About Sign Up Form

Sign Up Form is a complete registration form for React with name, email, password, confirm password and terms fields, built with Framer Motion and Tailwind CSS. Errors only appear once a field has been left, then clear as soon as it is fixed, so nobody is flagged while still typing. It includes a password reveal toggle, a length-weighted strength meter and a submit button that moves through loading, success and error states from the promise you return.

When to use it
A SaaS product needs a ready sign-up page that validates politely without extra libraries.
An onboarding flow wants a password strength hint that rewards length over symbol rules.
A landing page collects accounts and needs clear loading and failure feedback on submit.
Accessibility

Each field has a visible label and a suitable autocomplete value, invalid fields set aria-invalid and point to their error message, and errors render with the alert role so they are announced. The strength label updates in a polite live region, the reveal button is labelled "Show password" or "Hide password", and a form-level error message is linked to the submit button. With reduced motion enabled, messages and the strength meter fade without sliding or blurring.

FAQ
How do I make a sign up form in React?
Install the block and render SignUpForm with an onSubmit handler. onSubmit only receives valid values, and if it returns a promise the button shows loading, then success or error when it settles.
Can I use my own validation, such as a schema library?
Yes. Pass validate, a function that takes the values and returns an object with a message for each invalid field. It replaces the built-in rules.
How is password strength calculated?
The exported passwordStrength function scores mainly by length, with a small bonus for using three character types, and returns 0 to 4. Set strengthMeter to false to hide the meter.
Keep in mind

About Sign Up Form

Sign Up Form is a complete registration form for React with name, email, password, confirm password and terms fields, built with Framer Motion and Tailwind CSS. Errors only appear once a field has been left, then clear as soon as it is fixed, so nobody is flagged while still typing. It includes a password reveal toggle, a length-weighted strength meter and a submit button that moves through loading, success and error states from the promise you return.

When to use it
A SaaS product needs a ready sign-up page that validates politely without extra libraries.
An onboarding flow wants a password strength hint that rewards length over symbol rules.
A landing page collects accounts and needs clear loading and failure feedback on submit.
Accessibility

Each field has a visible label and a suitable autocomplete value, invalid fields set aria-invalid and point to their error message, and errors render with the alert role so they are announced. The strength label updates in a polite live region, the reveal button is labelled "Show password" or "Hide password", and a form-level error message is linked to the submit button. With reduced motion enabled, messages and the strength meter fade without sliding or blurring.

FAQ
How do I make a sign up form in React?
Install the block and render SignUpForm with an onSubmit handler. onSubmit only receives valid values, and if it returns a promise the button shows loading, then success or error when it settles.
Can I use my own validation, such as a schema library?
Yes. Pass validate, a function that takes the values and returns an object with a message for each invalid field. It replaces the built-in rules.
How is password strength calculated?
The exported passwordStrength function scores mainly by length, with a small bonus for using three character types, and returns 0 to 4. Set strengthMeter to false to hide the meter.
Keep in mind

Some components on this site are inspired by or recreated from existing work across the web. I'm not here to take credit; just to learn, experiment, and sometimes push things a bit further. If something looks familiar and I forgot to mention you, reach out and I'll fix that right away.

It includes a password reveal toggle, a length-weighted strength meter and a submit button that moves through loading, success and error states from the promise you return.</p><h3 class="mt-6 font-medium text-foreground">When to use it</h3><ul class="mt-2 list-disc space-y-1.5 pl-5"><li>A SaaS product needs a ready sign-up page that validates politely without extra libraries.</li><li>An onboarding flow wants a password strength hint that rewards length over symbol rules.</li><li>A landing page collects accounts and needs clear loading and failure feedback on submit.</li></ul><h3 class="mt-6 font-medium text-foreground">Accessibility</h3><p class="mt-2">Each field has a visible label and a suitable autocomplete value, invalid fields set aria-invalid and point to their error message, and errors render with the alert role so they are announced. With reduced motion enabled, messages and the strength meter fade without sliding or blurring.</p><h3 class="mt-6 font-medium text-foreground">FAQ</h3><dl class="mt-2 space-y-4"><div><dt class="font-medium text-foreground">How do I make a sign up form in React?</dt><dd class="mt-1">Install the block and render SignUpForm with an onSubmit handler. onSubmit only receives valid values, and if it returns a promise the button shows loading, then success or error when it settles.</dd></div><div><dt class="font-medium text-foreground">Can I use my own validation, such as a schema library?</dt><dd class="mt-1">Yes. An interactive project folder that opens its file fan on hover or focus, expands into a focus-managed overlay, then retraces the complete path when closed.

About Sign Up Form

Sign Up Form is a complete registration form for React with name, email, password, confirm password and terms fields, built with Framer Motion and Tailwind CSS. Errors only appear once a field has been left, then clear as soon as it is fixed, so nobody is flagged while still typing. It includes a password reveal toggle, a length-weighted strength meter and a submit button that moves through loading, success and error states from the promise you return.

When to use it
A SaaS product needs a ready sign-up page that validates politely without extra libraries.
An onboarding flow wants a password strength hint that rewards length over symbol rules.
A landing page collects accounts and needs clear loading and failure feedback on submit.
Accessibility

Each field has a visible label and a suitable autocomplete value, invalid fields set aria-invalid and point to their error message, and errors render with the alert role so they are announced. The strength label updates in a polite live region, the reveal button is labelled "Show password" or "Hide password", and a form-level error message is linked to the submit button. With reduced motion enabled, messages and the strength meter fade without sliding or blurring.

FAQ
How do I make a sign up form in React?
Install the block and render SignUpForm with an onSubmit handler. onSubmit only receives valid values, and if it returns a promise the button shows loading, then success or error when it settles.
Can I use my own validation, such as a schema library?
Yes. Pass validate, a function that takes the values and returns an object with a message for each invalid field. It replaces the built-in rules.
How is password strength calculated?
The exported passwordStrength function scores mainly by length, with a small bonus for using three character types, and returns 0 to 4. Set strengthMeter to false to hide the meter.
Keep in mind

Some components on this site are inspired by or recreated from existing work across the web. I'm not here to take credit; just to learn, experiment, and sometimes push things a bit further. If something looks familiar and I forgot to mention you, reach out and I'll fix that right away.

It includes a password reveal toggle, a length-weighted strength meter and a submit button that moves through loading, success and error states from the promise you return.</p><h3 class="mt-6 font-medium text-foreground">When to use it</h3><ul class="mt-2 list-disc space-y-1.5 pl-5"><li>A SaaS product needs a ready sign-up page that validates politely without extra libraries.</li><li>An onboarding flow wants a password strength hint that rewards length over symbol rules.</li><li>A landing page collects accounts and needs clear loading and failure feedback on submit.</li></ul><h3 class="mt-6 font-medium text-foreground">Accessibility</h3><p class="mt-2">Each field has a visible label and a suitable autocomplete value, invalid fields set aria-invalid and point to their error message, and errors render with the alert role so they are announced. With reduced motion enabled, messages and the strength meter fade without sliding or blurring.</p><h3 class="mt-6 font-medium text-foreground">FAQ</h3><dl class="mt-2 space-y-4"><div><dt class="font-medium text-foreground">How do I make a sign up form in React?</dt><dd class="mt-1">Install the block and render SignUpForm with an onSubmit handler. onSubmit only receives valid values, and if it returns a promise the button shows loading, then success or error when it settles.</dd></div><div><dt class="font-medium text-foreground">Can I use my own validation, such as a schema library?</dt><dd class="mt-1">Yes. An interactive project folder that opens its file fan on hover or focus, expands into a focus-managed overlay, then retraces the complete path when closed.

About Sign Up Form

Sign Up Form is a complete registration form for React with name, email, password, confirm password and terms fields, built with Framer Motion and Tailwind CSS. Errors only appear once a field has been left, then clear as soon as it is fixed, so nobody is flagged while still typing. It includes a password reveal toggle, a length-weighted strength meter and a submit button that moves through loading, success and error states from the promise you return.

When to use it
A SaaS product needs a ready sign-up page that validates politely without extra libraries.
An onboarding flow wants a password strength hint that rewards length over symbol rules.
A landing page collects accounts and needs clear loading and failure feedback on submit.
Accessibility

Each field has a visible label and a suitable autocomplete value, invalid fields set aria-invalid and point to their error message, and errors render with the alert role so they are announced. The strength label updates in a polite live region, the reveal button is labelled "Show password" or "Hide password", and a form-level error message is linked to the submit button. With reduced motion enabled, messages and the strength meter fade without sliding or blurring.

FAQ
How do I make a sign up form in React?
Install the block and render SignUpForm with an onSubmit handler. onSubmit only receives valid values, and if it returns a promise the button shows loading, then success or error when it settles.
Can I use my own validation, such as a schema library?
Yes. Pass validate, a function that takes the values and returns an object with a message for each invalid field. It replaces the built-in rules.
How is password strength calculated?
The exported passwordStrength function scores mainly by length, with a small bonus for using three character types, and returns 0 to 4. Set strengthMeter to false to hide the meter.
Keep in mind

Some components on this site are inspired by or recreated from existing work across the web. I'm not here to take credit; just to learn, experiment, and sometimes push things a bit further. If something looks familiar and I forgot to mention you, reach out and I'll fix that right away.

It includes a password reveal toggle, a length-weighted strength meter and a submit button that moves through loading, success and error states from the promise you return.</p><h3 class="mt-6 font-medium text-foreground">When to use it</h3><ul class="mt-2 list-disc space-y-1.5 pl-5"><li>A SaaS product needs a ready sign-up page that validates politely without extra libraries.</li><li>An onboarding flow wants a password strength hint that rewards length over symbol rules.</li><li>A landing page collects accounts and needs clear loading and failure feedback on submit.</li></ul><h3 class="mt-6 font-medium text-foreground">Accessibility</h3><p class="mt-2">Each field has a visible label and a suitable autocomplete value, invalid fields set aria-invalid and point to their error message, and errors render with the alert role so they are announced. With reduced motion enabled, messages and the strength meter fade without sliding or blurring.</p><h3 class="mt-6 font-medium text-foreground">FAQ</h3><dl class="mt-2 space-y-4"><div><dt class="font-medium text-foreground">How do I make a sign up form in React?</dt><dd class="mt-1">Install the block and render SignUpForm with an onSubmit handler. onSubmit only receives valid values, and if it returns a promise the button shows loading, then success or error when it settles.</dd></div><div><dt class="font-medium text-foreground">Can I use my own validation, such as a schema library?</dt><dd class="mt-1">Yes. Sign Up Form is a complete registration form for React with name, email, password, confirm password and terms fields, built with Framer Motion and Tailwind CSS. Errors only appear once a field has been left, then clear as soon as it is fixed, so nobody is flagged while still typing. It includes a password reveal toggle, a length-weighted strength meter and a submit button that moves through loading, success and error states from the promise you return.When to use itA SaaS product needs a ready sign-up page that validates politely without extra libraries.An onboarding flow wants a password strength hint that rewards length over symbol rules.A landing page collects accounts and needs clear loading and failure feedback on submit.AccessibilityEach field has a visible label and a suitable autocomplete value, invalid fields set aria-invalid and point to their error message, and errors render with the alert role so they are announced. The strength label updates in a polite live region, the reveal button is labelled "Show password" or "Hide password", and a form-level error message is linked to the submit button. With reduced motion enabled, messages and the strength meter fade without sliding or blurring.FAQHow do I make a sign up form in React?Install the block and render SignUpForm with an onSubmit handler. onSubmit only receives valid values, and if it returns a promise the button shows loading, then success or error when it settles.Can I use my own validation, such as a schema library?Yes. Pass validate, a function that takes the values and returns an object with a message for each invalid field. It replaces the built-in rules.How is password strength calculated?The exported passwordStrength function scores mainly by length, with a small bonus for using three character types, and returns 0 to 4. Set strengthMeter to false to hide the meter.
